findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison coordinate contrasts at the observed selection nodes are strongest for the short-range pair kernels: pair_kernel_1.5 (endpoint_effects:9, integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (endpoint_effects:10, z 0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (endpoint_effects:11, z 0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (endpoint_effects:12, z 0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (endpoint_effects:13, z -0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0). The same ordering appears in the branch-adjusted raw and adjusted covariance/correlation rows (branch_adjusted:163,164,240,241,86,87), so the enrichment is not an artifact of the branch adjustment. These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a radial pair-distance shell density, not an absolute geometric descriptor and not an interaction energy.

Global shape contrasts are signed and mostly negative: shape_yy is the strongest (endpoint_effects:4, z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0), with shape_xx (endpoint_effects:3, z -0.495, q 8.1e-4), shape_yz (endpoint_effects:8, z -0.212, q 0.035) and shape_zz (endpoint_effects:5, z -0.183, q 0.067) weaker. The branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlation rows for shape_yy (branch_adjusted:158,235) and the adjusted covariance rows for shape_yy/shape_yz (branch_adjusted:81,85) retain the same sign, so the shape signal is not removed by the branch adjustment. Shape entries are coordinate covariance descriptors in A^2, not a physical energy or a causal mechanism.

Global centroid contrasts are weak and not consistently signed: global_centroid_y is the only centroid term with q below 0.05 (endpoint_effects:1, z -0.243, q 0.014, positive batch fraction 0.214), while global_centroid_x (endpoint_effects:0, z -0.111, q 0.257) and global_centroid_z (endpoint_effects:2, z -0.061, q 0.481) are not distinguishable from zero at the supplied multiplicity. The branch-adjusted raw and adjusted covariance/correlation rows for the centroid (branch_adjusted:77,78,79,154,155,156) are likewise weak, so the centroid is not a supported priority relative to the pair-kernel and shape terms.

Landmark terms split by observable type. Softmin distances (lower = closer) are negative for landmark_00 (endpoint_effects:14, z -0.481, q 8.1e-4), landmark_04 (endpoint_effects:26, z -0.351, q 0.014), landmark_06 (endpoint_effects:32, z 0.294, q 6.8e-4), landmark_18 (endpoint_effects:68, z 0.264, q 6.0e-3) and landmark_19 (endpoint_effects:71, z -0.075, q 0.257), while occupancy3/occupancy5 shell densities are positive for landmark_00 (endpoint_effects:15, z 0.545, q 2.4e-4; endpoint_effects:16, z 0.208, q 0.020) and negative for landmark_01, 02, 03, 05, 06, 15, 18 (endpoint_effects:19,22,25,31,34,61,70). Occupancy is a radial shell density peaking at a=3 or 5 A, not an atom count and not monotone in distance, so the sign of an occupancy contrast cannot be read as a simple approach/retreat direction.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolations over the complete observed support [0.0, 0.49] with extrapolation_allowed=false and polynomial_accepted=false for every row. They show many sign changes (e.g. continuous:0 landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes and 1 strong sign conflict; continuous:1 landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts; continuous:17 landmark_01_local_cxy has 7 sign changes and 18 strong sign conflicts) and large first-to-last rate reversals (continuous:1 first_rate_z -17.49, last_rate_z 8.11; continuous:2 first_rate_z -72.37, last_rate_z 5.52). A constant rule is therefore not supported by these curves; a time-conditioned rule would have to be justified by validated fits or observed-node interpolation, and the curves are contrasts, not an absolute reward target.

The curve-fidelity audit in curve_support reports relative_node_rmse between about 0.386 and 0.931 and quiet_node_large_fit_fraction between 0.08 and 0.34 across the audited features, with strong_sign_conflict_nodes up to 15 (landmark_16_occupancy5). The selection rule retained 24 of the audited features under relative_rmse_le 0.35, strong_sign_conflict_nodes_eq 0 and quiet_node_large_fit_fraction_le 0.1, so the retained set is a filtered subset and the excluded features are not validated for a time-conditioned rule. Legendre runtime use is disallowed (legendre_runtime_allowed=false) for all audited features.

Descendant survival credit is available as survival_enrichment_z over 14 independent batches, but it is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity. The strongest survival terms are landmark_05_local_czz (survival_effects:56, z -0.419, q 0.120), landmark_15_local_czz (survival_effects:156, z -0.399, q 0.155), landmark_09_local_czz (survival_effects:96, z -0.390, q 0.120), landmark_05_local_cxx (survival_effects:54, z -0.383, q 0.302) and landmark_16_local_cyy (survival_effects:165, z -0.317, q 0.219); landmark_00_soft_mass is positive (survival_effects:0, z 0.365, q 0.120). None of these survival q-values is below 0.05, so the survival evidence does not by itself establish a final-affinity benefit, and the comparison with the endpoint contrasts is a comparison of different label semantics.

Parent-child increment contrasts disagree in sign with the endpoint contrasts for several features: landmark_00_softmin increment is negative (increment_effects:14, z -4.914, q 0.046) while the endpoint contrast is also negative (endpoint_effects:14), and landmark_00_occupancy3 increment is positive (increment_effects:15, z 4.277, q 0.081) matching the positive endpoint contrast (endpoint_effects:15). Shape_xx and shape_yy increments are negative (increment_effects:3, z -3.698, q 0.095; increment_effects:4, z -3.845, q 0.161) consistent with the negative endpoint shape contrasts, while shape_xz increment is positive (increment_effects:7, z 3.004, q 0.207) against a positive endpoint contrast (endpoint_effects:7). The increment table is a within-path change diagnostic; it does not by itself separate within-path change from changing cohort composition.

The turnover accounting separates population_rate, edge_rate and turnover_residual_rate. For landmark_00_soft_mass the edge rate is positive (turnover:1, z 4.545, p 0.034) while the turnover residual is negative (turnover:2, z -4.360, p 0.034), and for landmark_00_local_cxx the edge rate is negative (turnover:13, z -4.343, p 0.004) while the residual is positive (turnover:14, z 4.286, p 0.002). Large positive residuals also appear for landmark_01_local_cyy (turnover:47, z 6.397, q 0.014), landmark_04_local_cxx (turnover:134, z 5.671, q 0.012), landmark_07_local_cxx (turnover:224, z 5.076, q 0.012), landmark_07_local_cyy (turnover:227, z 5.633, q 0.019), landmark_08_local_cxx (turnover:254, z 5.543, q 0.012), landmark_16_local_cyy (turnover:497, z 6.367, q 0.012), landmark_17_local_cxx (turnover:524, z 5.244, q 0.012), landmark_19_local_cxx (turnover:584, z 5.298, q 0.012) and landmark_19_local_cyy (turnover:587, z 5.368, q 0.031). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

Joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with innovation_native_alignment (joint_diagnostics:1, mean 0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and with teacher_innovation_contrast_alignment (joint_diagnostics:11, mean 0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0), and negatively associated with observed_child_score_gain (joint_diagnostics:2, mean -0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast is dominated by its internal fraction (joint_diagnostics:14, mean 0.787) with smaller translation (joint_diagnostics:12, mean 0.132) and rotation (joint_diagnostics:13, mean 0.081) fractions. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit; they do not establish that a region adds information beyond common motion, and the negative child-score-gain association is a caution against reading selection innovation as a quality benefit.

Joint-motion terms are consistently negative and survive the branch adjustment: joint_innovation_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:74, raw covariance z -5.15e-5, q 0.038; branch_adjusted:151, adjusted covariance z -3.60e-5, q 0.020; branch_adjusted:228, raw correlation z -0.142, q 9.3e-5; branch_adjusted:305, adjusted correlation z -0.150, q 2.8e-4), joint_internal_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:76, q 0.044; branch_adjusted:153, q 0.030; branch_adjusted:230, q 1.5e-4; branch_adjusted:307, q 9.7e-4) and joint_translation_RMS_A (branch_adjusted:75, q 0.095; branch_adjusted:152, q 0.072; branch_adjusted:229, q 0.087; branch_adjusted:306, q 0.052). The internal component is the larger of the two, so the joint signal is not purely a rigid translation. These are coordinate RMS contrasts, not physical interaction energies.

The information audit reports compressed_choice_excess_fixed_RMS_A mean 0.081 (CI95 0.070-0.092), compressed_choice_fixed_RMS_A mean 0.564 (CI95 0.499-0.620), compressed_choice_proper_rigid_RMS_A mean 0.529 (CI95 0.468-0.582), top4_teacher_overlap mean 0.470 (CI95 0.427-0.515), compressed_chosen_teacher_score_correlation mean 0.102 (CI95 0.065-0.140) and full_chosen_teacher_score_correlation mean 0.064 (CI95 0.021-0.103), over 14 independent batches. The audit's own limitations state that the nonnegative excess distance is by construction and not a causal affinity effect, that proper rigid alignment retains fixed Hungarian correspondence, and that teacher score correlations are observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor. The remaining joint diagnostics (joint_diagnostics:0,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10) are descriptive within-selector associations with null_tested=false and no q-value.

hypotheses.claim: Hypothesis: the short-range pair-distance shell density (pair_kernel_1.5-3.5) is the most reproducible signed coordinate contrast at the observed selection nodes, and the sign reversal at pair_kernel_7.0 indicates that the contrast is not a monotone function of pair distance. A discriminating failure condition would be a re-run in which the pair_kernel_1.5-3.5 endpoint contrasts lose their positive batch fraction or the pair_kernel_7.0 contrast loses its negative sign.

Hypothesis: the landmark_00 local contrast curves are non-monotone over the observed window, with early and late rate signs that differ, so a time-conditioned rule could in principle differ from a constant rule. The supplied evidence does not validate a specific time-conditioned rule: the curves are observed-node linear interpolations with extrapolation disallowed, the polynomial fits are not accepted, and the curve-fidelity audit shows relative_node_rmse up to 0.93 and strong sign conflicts. A discriminating failure condition would be a validated fit that reproduces the observed-node values within the audited relative_node_rmse bound.

Hypothesis: immediate selection evidence and descendant survival credit disagree in direction for some landmark terms (for example landmark_00_softmin is negative in both the endpoint and increment tables while landmark_00_soft_mass is positive in survival credit), which would make direction priorities depend on which label semantics is used. The comparison is not decidable from the supplied evidence because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable and the survival table is recorded joint-head credit, not final affinity benefit.

Hypothesis: the joint-motion terms (joint_innovation_RMS_A, joint_internal_RMS_A) carry information beyond a common rigid translation, because the internal component is larger than the translation component and both survive the branch adjustment. The supplied evidence does not establish that any specific region adds information beyond common motion; the joint diagnostics are descriptive within-selector associations and the branch-adjusted rows are coordinate RMS contrasts. A discriminating failure condition would be a joint diagnostic in which the internal fraction collapses to the translation fraction.

Hypothesis: the large positive turnover residuals for the local_cxx and local_cyy terms at many landmarks indicate that within-path change and changing cohort composition contribute differently to the population rate, with the residual carrying the reclassification and parent-weighting component. The residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect, so this hypothesis is descriptive and would need a separate design to be tested.

Hypothesis: the compressed-choice excess distance and the teacher-overlap metrics are consistent with a selection process that is only weakly aligned with the teacher score, since the chosen-teacher score correlations are small (0.064-0.102) and the top4 teacher overlap is about 0.47. The audit explicitly states that the nonnegative excess distance is by construction and not a causal affinity effect, so this hypothesis is about the selection diagnostic, not about final affinity benefit.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling; it is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis is permitted.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term; moment effects, pair kernels and turnover rates are diagnostic evidence only.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed or evaluated here.
